text.title: Architect Skill Index (Geek Tier) — Worked Examples
text.summary: One complete 54-entry index over active dev, sdd and sdlc-ai methodologies, clustered by architecture activity, with a note on every choice a reader might question, and one five-entry draft that breaks five subject rules and what the validator and the reviewer say about it.

section.title: Scenario
section.p: The geek tier promises architects a single index over the existing sdlc-ai, dev and sdd entries. The first draft was a list of tool names with the targets' own summaries pasted under them. The editor runs steps 1-7 of `content/04-procedure.xml`, resolving every slug against its `meta.json`, and publishes the index below.

section.title: Good example: 54 entries in five activity clusters

example.title: Complete index with relink run
example.note: Every `est_tokens` is the value in the target's `meta.json` at the relink run, not an estimate: the relink script fails on a mismatch, which is what lets an agent trust the number when deciding whether to load a 5,000-token target.

`task-spec-kit-three-step` and `task-plan-mode-locked-execution` sit under "Deciding and recording", not under a "spec-kit" or "plan-mode" cluster: the architect's task is fixing the architecture before agents generate code, and that is the activity the cluster is named after.

`architect_why` for `c4-drift-detection-from-iac` is "diffs the C4 model against applied IaC state so the diagram reports its own drift" rather than the target's summary "produces a drift report comparing the canonical C4 diagram against the live Terraform state": the sentence names the governance task, and a reviewer diffing the two sees no paraphrase.

`entry_count` is 54, so no `shortfall` block is present; the schema only demands one below 50. The three `uncovered_tasks` are real gaps found while clustering, with the closest partial match named where one exists.

`relink.next_due` is three months after `last_run`, one review cadence; the run URL appears both in `relink` and in `evidence[]` because the rule requires the evidence link and the object is what the next run compares against.

example.title: Five subject rules broken
example.note: What the validator prints: `clusters[0].name: 'spec-kit' matches the forbidden not schema` and the same for `plan-mode` (r-clustered-by-architecture-activity); `clusters[0].entries[1].architect_why: 'Useful for architects.' matches the forbidden not schema` and `length 22 is under minLength 40` (r-architect-why-not-copied-summary); `clusters[0].entries[2].target_status: 'draft' is not the required const 'active'` (r-entry-resolves-to-existing-slug); `clusters[1].entries[1]: missing required field: load_when` (r-entry-fields-fixed); `clusters[1]: 2 items is under minItems 3`; `<root>: missing required field: shortfall` because entry_count 5 is under 50 (r-minimum-fifty-distinct-targets); `uncovered_tasks: 0 items is under minItems 1` (r-uncovered-tasks-listed).

What the reviewer sees beyond the validator: `task-plan-mode-locked-execution` appears under both clusters with two different est_tokens values (5100 and 4000), so at least one is not the meta.json figure and the slug is counted twice — fm-padding-to-fifty and fm-no-load-signal in one entry. The first `architect_why` is the target's summary verbatim. The draft goes back to step 1.

list.item: Resolve first, write second: an architect_why written for a slug that turns out to be draft is wasted, and a relink script makes resolution a build step rather than a chore.
The activity name is the index: an architect arrives with "I have to review a boundary change", and only a cluster named for that activity answers without prior knowledge of the tools.
An honest 47 with a shortfall block beats a padded 50; the uncovered-tasks section is where the next methodology request comes from.
